why: Prevent texture filtering from sampling adjacent road/biome cells when the terrain atlas is scaled.
implementation: Copy the selected atlas cell at native size into a temporary isolated canvas before repeated scaled draws; release it after painting and use the caller surface factory for worker compatibility.

pixelOracle.coverage: Both land and road selections; all regional rows. Nine million fully opaque central pixels per case compared against independently rendered flat expected quadrant color and established land tint.
pixelOracle.candidate: Zero unexpected pixels in each case.

workerRegression: Six actual-art pixel comparisons across all three biomes, roads/no-roads and river variants; obsolete task cancellation, undo/reuse, late result rejection, thumbnail reuse, capability fallback and nine worker lifecycle/error paths pass.

publicJourney.observed: Three regular-player biome selections, frozen saved maps, regional planting, native playtest climate and return to editor; no page errors.

natureReview.findings: No additional clipping, displaced targets or scale mismatch noticed in these three boards. Existing fine-ground competition persists.

limits: Atlas isolation fixes sampled-color contamination, not the broader terrain artwork hierarchy, tiling repetition or all landscape art gates.
Only listed boards and five full gameplay scenes were visually inspected after this source change.
No new performance or memory acceptance claim; no raster replacement integrated.
